thread:
DeployBot: Canary rollout started: prod/v2-infer -> us-west-2 (canary 10%). tracking_id=deploy-881. health checks enabled.

IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v2/stream endpoints in us-west-2 canary. 3m avg 5xx = 6.8% (threshold 2%). paging oncall.

Aisha (oncall): seeing pager, joining. what symptoms? are we seeing latency or pure errors?

Tom (sre): errors seem to be 503s from inference-runtime-gateway -> model-worker. stack traces show OOM eviction logs in worker pod. hit during long context requests.

Renee (prod-eng): Confirmed from canary logs. Most failing requests are streaming multi-turn sessions (>1500 tokens). Non-stream endpoints mostly OK.

Aisha (oncall): ok. abort criteria in rollout doc: if 5xx > 5% for 5m OR customer-facing latency > 300ms P95 for 2m => abort. We hit 5% threshold. Initiating soft-stop.

Tom (sre): initiating prefix route isolation to divert new canary traffic to fallback model variant (v2-infer-quant) as temporary mitigation. Running command:

```
# route isolation
kubectl -n infra exec -it router-ctl -- ./routectl promote --route v2-infer -> v2-infer-quant --scope canary
```

Renee (prod-eng): doing feature-flag kill-switch on canary rollout flag (rollout.v2_infer). toggling now.

Aisha (oncall): please confirm when flag toggled and whether we should pause then roll back.

Renee (prod-eng): FLAG: rollout.v2_infer -> OFF. Verified in flags dashboard. Canary traffic should stop within 15s.

Tom (sre): saw immediate drop in new 5xx. However backlog of inflight streams still generating 503s. Spawning script to drain workers gracefully.

Aisha (oncall): customer impact: Monitoring product tier shows a small set of paying accounts experienced partial stream failures (estimated ~120 distinct sessions in last 10m). No data loss reported; responses retried by client in many cases. Notifying CS.

Renee (prod-eng): initiating rollback to previous model variant for canary nodes. Command: `/deploy rollback --id deploy-881 --target v1-infer-stable`

DeployBot: Rollback started for deploy-881. ETA 5m. Will route canary traffic back to v1-infer-stable.

Tom (sre): draining script output:
```
drain-workers --canary --grace 60
drain: worker-27 -> ok
drain: worker-28 -> evicted, restarting
drain: worker-29 -> ok
```

IncidentBot: NOTE: Pager duty escalation suppressed (mitigated) because rollback in progress.

Aisha (oncall): Renee, after rollback completes, can you run a quick regression eval on a 50 prompt sample to ensure quality parity? Also capture broken request ids for triage.

Renee (prod-eng): on it. starting eval harness now. collecting request ids: 0f3a9c, 4b7e2d, 9c1f20... will attach log bundle to incident ticket.

Tom (sre): rollback complete. all canary nodes now on v1-infer-stable. 5xx rate back to baseline (0.6%). P95 latency back to normal.

Aisha (oncall): Good. Notifying affected customers via CS with summary. Creating follow-up incident for RCA and remediation items (OOM during long streaming sessions). Potential fixes: worker memory tuning, pre-splitting long-context requests, safer default quant variant for canary, add load-shedding for long streaming sessions.

Renee (prod-eng): Agree. I'll open a PR for canary gating: disallow rollout to canary for models that haven't passed long-context mem benchmark.

Aisha (oncall): Handoff to oncall backup for postmortem: @Tom taking lead for next 24h. I'll continue monitoring for 1h then sign off.

Tom (sre): ack. I'll collect metrics, heap dumps from evicted workers, and coordinate postmortem.

Renee (prod-eng): attaching quick repro command for devs:
```
# repro long stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @long_session.json https://api.redwood.ai/v2/stream
```

Aisha (oncall): thanks everyone. closing this thread when ticket is created. IncidentBot: create incident ticket with label canary-oom-streaming and link to logs.

IncidentBot: Incident ticket INC-2026-881 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-881

Aisha (oncall): thread closed for now. Follow-ups in INC-2026-881. :white_check_mark:
